title: Fix useJobs.ts — toUpperCase on never type in exhaustive switch
description:
**File:** `dashboard/src/hooks/useJobs.ts`

**Problem:** Line 52: `return state.toUpperCase()` in the default case of an exhaustive switch. TypeScript correctly infers the type as `never` since all `JobStatus` values are explicitly handled in cases above. TypeScript error TS2339.

**Fix:** Cast to string as a safety-net fallback:
```typescript
default:
  return (state as string).toUpperCase();
```

This handles any future `JobStatus` values that haven't been added to the switch yet, while satisfying TypeScript.
definitionOfDone: TypeScript error TS2339 in useJobs.ts is resolved
stateToBackend still correctly maps all known JobStatus values

implementationPlan.description: In useJobs.ts line 52, change `return state.toUpperCase()` to `return (state as string).toUpperCase()`. The switch is exhaustive over all known JobStatus values, so TypeScript infers `never` in the default branch. The cast makes this a safe fallback for any future JobStatus values added to the union without updating this switch.
Run `node ./node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit` and verify TS2339 error is gone for useJobs.ts.
